primitives.name: Neon gse-postgres
primitives.verbatim_quote: | Asset | Why | Reality | |-------|-----|---------| | Neon gse-postgres | Prod DB + branching
primitives.assumptions: (1) Production database workload; (2) Neon's serverless architecture eliminates infrastructure management; (3) Branching provides isolated development environments; (4) pgvector enables similarity search for high-dimensional embeddings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Single point of truth (SoT) failure occurs when Neon's URL endpoints become stale due to instance rotation, requiring manual verification against the Neon console.

layer2.mapping: The Neon database serves as the foundational state-transition kernel in GSE, analogous to how GSI's probabilistic models map observed data to predictive distributions. Both systems rely on a single authoritative source: Neon for relational/pgvector data, and GSI's conformal inference pipelines for sports outcome probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Verify database connection latency < 100ms and check Neon's console for active instance status to ensure continuous SoT availability.

primitives.name: Vercel sports-web
primitives.verbatim_quote: | SoT; set pooled + unpooled URLs | | Vercel sports-web | Next.js prod | Env
primitives.assumptions: (1) Serverless function execution; (2) Environment variable security; (3) Automatic scaling based on traffic demand; (4) Continuous deployment from Git branch.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Configuration drift occurs when environment variables are updated but not redeployed, leading to runtime errors or security leaks.

layer2.mapping: Vercel's edge functions serve as the real-time decision-making layer in GSE, processing incoming HTTP requests and returning dynamic content. This mirrors GSI's online learning algorithms that update predictive models with new streaming data, both requiring immediate consistency between code and configuration.
layer2.telemetry: Monitor Vercel dashboard for successful builds and track request latencies to detect misconfiguration-induced slowdowns.

primitives.name: Prisma dual URL
primitives.verbatim_quote: after changes | | Prisma dual URL | Migrations vs runtime pool | DATABASE_URL + DIRECT_URL
primitives.assumptions: (1) DATABASE_URL for migrations ensures schema consistency; (2) DIRECT_URL bypasses connection pooling for direct writes; (3) Both URLs share the same underlying database cluster.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Schema divergence happens when migrations target DATABASE_URL but runtime queries use DIRECT_URL, causing type mismatches or missing tables.

layer2.mapping: The dual URL pattern implements a separation-of-concerns duality similar to GSI's train-test split methodology: DATABASE_URL acts as the training dataset for schema evolution, while DIRECT_URL serves as the test/validation endpoint for production integrity checks, ensuring model generalization to live traffic.
layer2.telemetry: Run periodic schema diff checks between DATABASE_URL and the database cluster to catch unsynchronized migrations.

primitives.name: LiteLLM multi-provider
primitives.verbatim_quote: LiteLLM | Multi-provider spend control | Stand up after free keys | --## Tier 1 —
primitives.assumptions: (1) Provider switching is automatic based on cost/performance; (2) API key rotation is handled internally; (3) Usage quotas are enforced per provider.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Provider outage causes fallback cascades, potentially degrading response quality or exhausting primary provider budgets during failover.

layer2.mapping: LiteLLM's routing logic implements a multi-armed bandit selection process, similar to GSI's ensemble model weighting where each provider/model arm contributes to the final prediction distribution. Both systems optimize cumulative reward (lower cost or higher accuracy) over time.
layer2.telemetry: Track monthly spend by provider and monitor success rates to identify underperforming APIs for replacement.
